artworks.title: The Death of Procris
artworks.description: Piero's National Gallery panel: Procris lies by the shore, slain by the unerring javelin she gave Cephalus — love undone by suspicion.

artworks.title: Cephalus and Procris
artworks.description: Veronese's Strasbourg canvas: the hunter cradles dying Procris among dogs and foliage — the fatal throw of the never-missing spear.

artworks.title: Landscape with Cephalus and Procris Reunited by Diana
artworks.description: Claude's National Gallery light: Diana reconciles the couple and bestows the hound and javelin that will later doom them.

artworks.title: Cephalus and Procris (The Death of Procris)
artworks.description: Wtewael's Mannerist collapse: Procris dies in Cephalus' arms in the forest — mistrust ending in irreversible loss.

popCulture.title: Cephalus
popCulture.description: The hunter whose javelin never misses — and who kills Procris by mistake when jealousy sends her into the brush.

popCulture.title: Procris
popCulture.description: The wife who dies testing her husband's fidelity — Ovid's emblem of love destroyed by suspicion.
